agent.result_text:
Holds now count in every total again. The only thing a hold still does is in the pools: a held person gets no cut, and their share is spread over the others. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What changed**
- **Server** (`ClaimFigures.java`): there's one check that decides when an open or pending claim is left out of a live total. It used to drop a claim if it was held, or if a hold of its person's covered its date. Now it only drops a claim once its person's retirement date has been reached. Due-totals, overdue, the period figures, statements and the rollup lines all go through that check, so they all count held claims again. Claimed already counted them and is unchanged.
- **Front end** (`claims.ts`): the same check made the same way, so the on-screen totals match the server. This covers due-totals, overdue, aged, months, tags, splits, the period figures and the classic summary.
- **Pools**: not touched. `RespondWithPools.java` still checks holds itself to decide who gets a cut.
- **Cleanup**: I deleted `Person.leftOn`, which nothing used any more. I also rewrote the code comments that still said a held claim "counts in no live total".

No stored data, schema, `data-testid` or audit records changed. My last edit was a comment in `TakeStatement.java`, made after the passing run; I didn't run the tests again for it.

probe.probe_text:
Nothing was changed. I read the core calculation code, the claim status rules and the front end myself; three helper agents read the rest of the Java back end. # 1. Figures and the rules behind them ## Where the numbers come from Nearly every money figure on the screen is calculated **in the browser**. The server sends plain claims, people, rates and settings, and the front end works out every due and total from them. The server has its own copy of the same rules in `claim/ClaimFigures.java`. It uses that copy when it freezes a figure: when a claim is settled, re-settled or part-settled, when a statement is taken, when a period is closed, and for the rollup, snapshot and alert audit lines. | Server | Browser | |---|---| | `ClaimFigures.due` / `figure` / `lateCharge` / `floored` / `rounding` / `lateFrom` / `overdue` | `rates.ts`: `chargedOf` / `figureOf` / `dueOf` / `atLeast` / `roundsHalfUp`; `claims.ts`: `lateFromOf` / `isOverdue` | | `ClaimFigures.counts` / `countsLive` / `countsClaimed` / `countsAsOf` | `claims.ts`: `counts` / `countsLive` / `countsClaimed` / `countsAsOf` | | `ClaimFigures.dueTotal` (with the cap) | `rates/due.slot.tsx`: `personDue` / `personExcess` / `personFigures` | | `ClaimFigures.rateOn`, `Rate.forClaim` | `rates.ts`: `rateOn` / `rateForClaim` | | `Sheet.floorOn`, `latePctOn`, `roundingOn`, … | `roles.ts`: `settingOn` | ## Shown on each claim row (`claims/list.slot.tsx`) - **claim-due** comes from `chargedOf` (server: `ClaimFigures.due`). It is taken from the first of these that applies: 1. **Frozen due** (`Claim.due`): set when the claim is settled. 2. **Bound figure** (`statedDue`): while the claim is bound by its person's last statement. 3. **Live figure**, worked out in four steps: - **Base:** amount × the rate percent ÷ 100. - The rate is for the grade the person had on the claim's date (`PersonGrades.on`), in force on that date. - It is looked up on this sheet first, then up the parent chain (`findInChain`: up to 3 parent levels, then the sheet it was cloned from). - If that rate's to-date is already past, there is none (`Rate.endedBy`). - A rate saved as forward-only (from-date on or after the sheet's today) does not apply to claims that existed before it (`Rate.forClaim` / `rateForClaim`). - With no rate, the due shows **n/a**. - **Rounding** to 2 decimals (`ClaimFigures.rounding` / `roundsHalfUp`): - If a `rounding` setting is in force on the claim's rounding date (`roundsOn`), it decides. - Otherwise the claim rounds half-up when dated before `policyDateInForce` (the policy date, or the sheet's today when blank), and half-to-even on or after it. - A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects (`correctsDate`). - **Floor:** the figure is raised to `floorOn(claim date)`, which defaults to 1.00. Corrections take no floor. - **Late charge** (`chargeByBoundary`): - For each full 30 days since `lateFrom` (the due-by plus the `grace-` days in force on the claim's date), it adds `latePctOn(boundary date)` × (floored figure + charges so far), rounded like the due. So it compounds. - There is none for a correction, a `waived` claim, or a claim that is not overdue. - **claim-overdue:** the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `lateFrom` is before the sheet's today. - **claim-due-by:** `fixDue` sets it when the claim is created: the `dueTerms`-th business day after `dueFrom`, skipping weekends and holidays (`BusinessDays.after`). - `dueTerms` is the person's own terms, else their grade's terms, else the sheet's (default 14). All are taken as in force on the sheet's today at creation (`Sheet.termsFor`). - Re-dating or editing the claim never changes it. Adding a holiday reworks it (`reworkDueBy`) on every claim that is not SETTLED or VOID. - **claim-period:** the period that contains the **due-by**, not the claim's date. - **claim-number:** given when the claim is opened (`ApplyClaimStatus`). - Normally `FY-`: the year is the fiscal year of the due-by, and the count is shared across the sheet's tree. - While `periodNumberingOn`, it is `-`, or `X-` when the due-by is in no period. - REVIEW claims get no number until a steward reviews them. Reassigning or splitting a claim gives it a new number. - **Other values shown on the row:** - status, stated, opened-by, corrects - deferred (the row's own `today < deferredUntil` test, which does not check that the claim is OPEN, unlike `isDeferred`) and deferred-until - proofs, receipts and photos - split-from, late-entry (added while the due-by's period was soft-closed), waived, held - reminded, ref, tags, batch - review-late (`reviewOn` plus `reviewSla` is before today) - lines, comments, log and timeline ## Shown on each person row - **person-due-total** (`personDue` / `ClaimFigures.dueTotal`): - Adds up the dues of the claims that pass `countsLive`: - OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED count; OPEN deferred past today does not. - Once the person's retirement date is reached, their unbound OPEN and PENDING claims drop out. - It is **n/a** when the person's grade today has no rate today, **unless** some counted claim keeps a figure: it is frozen, bound, live at another grade, or dated on or before today. - It is capped at `cap`, and **person-excess** shows the amount above the cap. - **person-claimed** (`sumOf` / `countsClaimed`): the sum of amounts, not dues. Corrections are left out. - **person-settled-total / person-open-total** (`splitOf`), **person-overdue-count / -total** (`overdueOf`), **person-aged-0-30 / 31-60 / 61** (by days since the claim's date), **person-active** (an OPEN or PENDING claim that counts, dated within the last 30 days). - **person-period-

-due-total / -carried** (`personPeriodDue` / `personPeriodCarried`): - Counted by the status each claim had at the end of the period (`statusOn` from the claim's status log), but valued at today's figure. - "Carried" covers claims whose due-by is in earlier periods and that were still OPEN or PENDING at that point, plus the person's opening balance. - Once the period is closed or soft-closed, the frozen `personTotals` / `personCarried` are shown instead. - **person-backing:** each patron's frozen dues on SETTLED claims dated in the last 90 days, times the patron's equal share (`sharesOf`), rounded half-to-even. - **person-cut-total** (pool cuts: see Holds below). - **Statement and snapshot figures:** statement-count, stated-total and statement-date, statement lines and snapshot lines are all frozen values from the server. - **Other values:** - grade (`gradeOn` today), terms, retired and retired-from, retirement lines - hold and hold lines, flag (shown while `flaggedOn`), approver - aliases, clashing, origin, tags, watched, contact ## Sheet-level totals - **rollup-due-total / header-due-total** (`trimmedSum`): with three or more people, the highest and the lowest are left out. - **classic-due-total:** the same sum with nothing left out. - **Overdue, claimed, settled/open and aged totals.** - **Period due-totals** (`periodDue`), and **classic period totals**, which count each claim by its status now rather than at the period's end. - **Month and tag totals.** - **crew-due-total:** the lead's and members' `personDue` added up. - **Consolidated totals:** the sheet plus all its descendant sheets, each with its own today, rates and settings. - **Dashboard and header counters** (the dashboard is shown only to stewards). ## What freezes a figure, and when - **Settle** (`ApplyClaimStatus`) freezes `due` at `ClaimFigures.due`, including any late charge on that day. - With `?on=` it freezes the due as it stood at the end of that date, rebuilt through `AsOf`. - When the due is n/a it stays live. - **Re-settle** (steward only) replaces the frozen due with `openDue`: today's rates and grades, ignoring any statement binding. - **Statement** (`TakeStatement`) binds every claim that passes `countsLive` to its current due (`stated` and `statedDue`) and unbinds all the others. - A bound claim's due stops following the sheet's today. - Reassigning, splitting or cancelling a statement unbinds the claim. Cancelling does not restore the previous statement's bindings. - **Closing or soft-closing a period** freezes `personTotals`, `personCarried` and `closedTotal`. Reopening clears them. - **Moving the sheet's today** writes a snapshot of each person's due-total for the day being left (`PersonSnapshot`). - **Fixed when the claim is created:** the due-by, its terms and `dueFrom`. ## Status rules and who may do what - **Status changes** (`ClaimStatus.after`): - DRAFT can be opened, voided or deleted. - OPEN can be settled or voided. - PENDING can be approved, rejected or voided. - SETTLED can be voided, but only by a steward, within 7 days of settling (`VOID_DAYS`). - DELETED can be restored, but only on the same sheet today it was deleted. - VOID is final. - **Opening:** - If the due is above `reviewThresholdOn(claim date)`, the claim goes to REVIEW instead, and only a steward can review it. - If the due is above `noteThresholdOn`, the claim needs a note. - A period cap refuses the open once the person already has that many OPEN or PENDING claims whose due-by is in the period. - For a flagged person, only a steward can open. - **Settling:** - The person who opened the claim, or last edited it, cannot settle or approve it. - A deferred claim cannot be settled. - Above `proofThresholdFor(grade, date)`, the claim needs a proof, and one of each kind in `proofKinds`. - A clerk settling above `clerkLimitFor(grade today)` leaves the claim PENDING instead. - Only a steward or the person's approver can approve or reject. A rejection needs a reason. - **Permissions** (`Sheet.allows`): the permission matrix decides open, settle, void, close, reassign and reopen. The standing rule lets clerk and steward open, settle, void and close; only a steward may reassign or reopen. - Hard-coded steward-only actions: waive, redate, resettle, flag, merge, transfer, archive, clone, cancel a statement, lock or unlock a period. - A delegation makes a user steward while the sheet's today falls inside it (`roleOf`). A viewer is refused every change (`GuardViewer`), and an archived sheet refuses every change (`GuardArchived`). - **What a date decides:** - The sheet's `today` replaces the clock everywhere. - The claim's date picks the grade, the rate, the floor and the thresholds. Its rounding date (`roundsOn`) picks the rounding. - The due-by picks the period, the closed check, the number and lateness. - `entryDateInForce` is the default date when adding a claim. - **Closed and soft-closed periods:** - A claim whose due-by is in a closed period cannot be added, edited, change status, be split, reassigned, re-settled, deferred or redated. - A soft-closed period still allows all of that, but marks new claims `lateEntry` and keeps its frozen totals. - With `graceDays` set, moving today auto-closes periods whose to-date plus the grace is before it (`AutoClosePeriods`). This skips the permission check. - **Holds:** - A claim's hold (`held`) or a person's hold takes **nothing** out of any total. - Its only effect: a person under a hold on today gets a 0.00 pool cut (`RespondWithPools`), and the others' shares are scaled up. - **Retirement:** - Claims dated after `retiredFrom`, or inside a past retirement, are refused (`retiredOn`). - From the day `retiredFrom` is reached, the person's unbound OPEN and PENDING claims leave every live total (`retiredBy`). - **Imports:** - Rates import (`importrates`): sets rates the same way the rate form does. - People import (`importpeople`): updates a matching person differently from the person form. - Openings import (`opening`): adds the balance to any already there, so pasting twice doubles it. - Paste box: matches existing drafts, adds the rest, then opens every line. - Plans: each generates claims through `ClaimRules.make`. ## Inconsistencies found along the way - **Holds:** several Javadoc and TS comments say held or hold-dated claims "do not count". These include `Person.java`, the comments on `overdueOf`, `isActive`, `periodDue` and `personDue`, and the `countsAsOf` Javadoc. The code counts them. - **Period due-total:** the comment in `periods.slot.tsx` says claims are grouped by their date; the code groups them by due-by. - **Terms used for the due-by:** `BuildClaim` and `ApplySplit` say terms "on its date"; the code uses the terms on the sheet's today. - **Blank date:** editing a claim defaults it to today, but adding one defaults it to the entry date. - **Transfer that merges:** it drops patrons and pool and crew memberships, unlike `ApplyMerge`. - **No role checks where you'd expect them:** any clerk can change settings, including the permission matrix, and can make themselves steward through `ApplyRole`. # 2. How hard it was to follow Hard. The core due calculation sits in one fairly readable class (`ClaimFigures`), but it is copied by hand into the browser (`rates.ts`, `claims.ts`, `due.slot.tsx`) and re-filtered differently in about a dozen screen pieces. Who-may-do-what and the closed-period checks are split between YAML step lists and inline checks in roughly 80 small step classes. Comments that no longer match the code (holds above all) make it easy for a new developer to believe the wrong rule.
